\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{চেঁচানো} (chẽchāno)}{চেঁচানো (chẽchāno)}]{\bn{চেঁচানো} (chẽchāno) — to shout}

\label{lesson:BN-C211-chechano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to marry, then the Bengali for to survive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{চেঁচানো}}
\textbf{\bn{চেঁচানো}} — \emph{chẽchāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to shout\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{চেঁচানো}} (\emph{chẽchāno}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*cicc}, \textquotedblleft{}scream\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 4789). CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{cẽcāna}, \textquotedblleft{}to cry out\textquotedblright{}, and calls the word imitative.
\end{cousinweb}
